description: Fixture corpus for the version 1 MCP interface: the tool responses of docs/MCP_SPEC.md sections 7.1, 7.4, 7.6 and 7.7 inside the common envelope of section 5. Valid cases must decode and re-encode to the byte string recorded in canonical.json; invalid cases must be refused with the recorded reason. Several invalid cases exist only to hold the trust contract of section 6 and ADR-0010: a response carrying page-derived or uploaded content is refused when it declares a trusted label, because a mislabelled response is the one an agent would act on.

valid.name: review-get-bugs-on-homepage
valid.note: The Stage 0 exit criterion in one document: an MCP client retrieved bugs-on-homepage by its project-scoped slug and received the review, a bounded page of findings, a cursor for the rest and evidence as links rather than bytes. The label is mixed, because the review title is a human instruction while the finding's URL came from a page.

valid.name: project-current
valid.note: Project, workspace and policy. agent_may_accept_findings is false and secret_tools_available is false, so the agent learns both boundaries from the first call rather than from a refusal.

valid.name: agent-session-status
valid.note: Session identity, the negotiated capability set including review_inbox: true, and the browser session with the control epoch a capture must present.

valid.name: browser-take-screenshot
valid.note: The after screenshot of the Stage 0 exit criterion: a verified artefact returned as a resource link with its digest, never as inline image bytes, and labelled untrusted_browser_content because it is a picture of a page.

valid.name: browser-session-start
valid.note: The allocated session an agent works from: its epoch, the lease it holds, and the one origin it may reach. No capability appears in it — the route capability is minted by the control plane and never leaves it.

valid.name: browser-navigate
valid.note: A navigation result. The settled URL, the status and the title all came from a page, so the response is labelled untrusted_browser_content.

valid.name: browser-snapshot
valid.note: The docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4 snapshot shape, whose element references are valid for this snapshot alone.

valid.name: finding-submit-verification
valid.note: A submitted verification with summary, branch, commit, tested viewports, checks and the after artefact. Its status is submitted and the finding is FIXED_UNVERIFIED: the agent has claimed a fix with evidence, and nothing here accepts it.

valid.name: finding-update-status-awaiting-human-review
valid.note: The terminal state available to an agent. There is no response in this corpus in which an agent moved a human-authored finding further, because the tool argument enumeration cannot express one.

valid.name: finding-get-degraded-without-image-content
valid.note: A client that declared no image capability. It still receives the annotation with its text label, the evidence link and its digest, plus a warning naming what it missed. Degradation is a warning on a success, not a failure (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.3).

invalid.name: not-json
invalid.note: Prose where a response was expected. A tool result is a document with a schema, not a sentence an agent parses by reading it.

invalid.name: unsupported-protocol-version
invalid.note: A future protocol version is refused rather than best-effort parsed (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 14).

invalid.name: unknown-tool
invalid.note: A secret tool, which Stage 0 does not expose at all. An unknown tool is rejected rather than dispatched to a default, so a response claiming to come from a tool this build does not have cannot be read.

invalid.name: envelope-with-unknown-property
invalid.note: An unknown envelope property. It carries a credential here to make the point concrete: additionalProperties false is what stops a response growing a field nobody agreed to, and docs/SECURITY.md section 18 is why that matters.

invalid.name: policy-allows-agent-acceptance
invalid.note: agent_may_accept_findings is a boolean. A string here would be truthy in JavaScript, which is exactly how an authority rule gets inverted by accident.

invalid.name: finding-without-untrusted-fields
invalid.note: untrusted_fields is required on every finding. A finding always carries the URL it was captured at, so a response that names no page-derived member is one that forgot to.

invalid.name: screenshot-labelled-trusted
invalid.note: A capture declaring trusted_control_plane. ADR-0010 forbids returning page content without an untrusted label, and the codec refuses it on the way out as well as on the way in.

invalid.name: browser-navigate-trusted-label
invalid.note: A navigation result under a trusted label. The page chose the URL and the title, so the codec refuses the label rather than the handler being trusted to set it.

invalid.name: review-findings-labelled-trusted
invalid.note: Findings under a trusted label, with an instruction planted in the captured URL. This is the shape a prompt-injection attempt would need to succeed, and it is refused before an agent sees it.
